analysis:
The changes are display-only and advisory, at the CLI level.

StatusCommand.swift head:148-153 now displays `displayedProviderAuthorization`, a presumably more lenient view that still shows App Attest while the lease is unexpired and a renewal is late. It separately computes `removalAuthorization` with the stricter `currentProviderAuthorization` and passes both to `ProviderAuthorizationReadiness.summary(_:removalAuthorization:now:)`. The new test at StatusCommandRunTests head:279-305 asserts that status does not offer MDM removal ('MDM removal needs fresh coordinator readiness', no 'run unenroll') when only the displayed authorization exists.

UnenrollCommand+KeepServing.swift head:21-27 and 61-66 still gate the removal guidance on `removalReady(currentProviderAuthorization)` at both checks. The summary call at head:24-25 only gains the `removalAuthorization` argument, passing the same value, so the gate is unchanged.

The relevant boundaries are TB-011, T-053 and T-057. Serving permission is coordinator-enforced, so the local status text does not grant routing. Premature MDM removal (T-057) remains gated by the stricter current authorization at two points in unenroll. No regression was identified.

Not visible in this batch: the implementations of `displayedProviderAuthorization`, `currentProviderAuthorization` and `summary(removalAuthorization:)`, which are likely in ProviderCore DaemonState and ProviderAuthorizationReadiness. Integration should verify three things:
- `displayedProviderAuthorization` is never used by any removal or serving gate.
- `summary` derives removal advice only from `removalAuthorization` (nil or not removalReady means no unenroll suggestion).
- The displayed view still rejects expired leases, a coordinator URL mismatch and revocation, so status cannot misstate trust after expiry (T-058 misstatement).
